none_fit.heading: The Beckham regime may not be the question your move turns on
none_fit.result_copy: The Beckham regime is a special tax treatment for people who BECOME Spanish tax residents because of a qualifying work reason — an employment contract or employer-ordered relocation, remote work for a foreign employer, a company directorship, a certified entrepreneurial activity, or highly qualified professional work. If none of those describes your move, the regime is not the right frame for your situation, and that is not the same as saying you have no Spanish tax question to answer. Retirees and people relocating on passive or investment income fall outside the regime entirely, because Article 93 targets inbound workers and their earned income. People already resident in Spain, or returning after a recent Spanish tax-residency period, run into the prior-residency condition rather than the work-reason one. In each of those cases the useful next step is ordinary Spanish residency and IRPF planning with a qualified gestor or asesor fiscal — and for a pension or investment profile, a wealth and pensions adviser rather than a Beckham specialist, because it is a different speciality.

insufficient_information.heading: Your Beckham position needs a closer look
insufficient_information.result_copy: Your answers do not yet establish whether the Beckham regime is available to you. Article 93 stacks several conditions and each one has to hold on its own: you must not have been a Spanish tax resident during any of the cinco períodos impositivos before your displacement; your move must be attributable to one of the qualifying work reasons; and the election itself must be made through Modelo 149 inside the statutory window. Any single one of those can decide the outcome by itself, and the two people most often get wrong are the prior-residency count — which turns on days present, the centre of your economic interests and your habitual residence, not on whether you felt settled — and the election deadline, which runs from Spanish social-security registration rather than from arrival or from your employment start date, and which is not extended by a late realisation that the regime existed. A short personalised review sets out which condition is actually in doubt for you and what evidence resolves it, while an application can still be made.
